decisions.reason: As a core, engineering-intensive resin injection unit with a dedicated launch presence and clear fit to our announced application-technology strategy, we would be inclined to continue it in 2022 and treat any weak uptake as temporary niche-market variation rather than abandon sunk development effort.

Because this second resin injection unit also received standalone presentation and sits squarely in our established competence base, escalation of commitment makes us likely to retain it and justify prior investment by expecting slower but recoverable demand.

The automatic airless spray gun is highly central to our longstanding spray-equipment business, so after publicly launching it on its own page we would likely keep it and interpret mixed results as normal adoption lag in industrial customer segments.

A manual airless spray gun is close to our core product family and distributor-supported installed base, which makes management prone to continue it in order to defend the prior commitment and preserve a broad solution portfolio for different customer specifications.

Since the air-assisted airless spray gun directly supports our strategy of innovative customized application technology and was visibly introduced to the market, we would be inclined to keep it and wait for demand to build rather than reverse course.

The data logger was quickly downgraded from its own page to a mere website mention, suggesting weaker market traction and lower strategic centrality than the core mechanical equipment lines, so even with escalation tendencies management would be more willing to discontinue it by 2022.
